patterns_found: A PostgreSQL session advisory lock is released when its database session ends, so an absent lock proves session loss but not owning-process death.
An OS-owned loopback socket stays live independently of PostgreSQL and closes when its owning process exits or releases the socket.
Binding port zero requests an OS-assigned port, and a same-address second-bind self-test can fail startup when the current host cannot provide exclusive Handshake-to-Handshake lease semantics.
PostgreSQL pg_temp can precede pg_catalog for relation lookup unless search_path is explicitly pinned; authority-table queries must resolve and pin the intended schema.
rejected_options: Timestamp-only orphan inference because it can close another live instance.
A permanent PostgreSQL session advisory lock as sole liveness proof because PostgreSQL restart, idle-session termination, or network loss releases it while the app can remain alive.
A filesystem PID/lock file because stale files, hardcoded paths, and cross-disk relocation weaken portability and crash proof.
Treating malformed or missing lease metadata as stale because unknown liveness must fail safe.
research_basis_v2.selected_approach: Hold a process-owned loopback UDP port lease from before reconciliation/artifact access through durable STOP drain; persist its versioned descriptor in every embedded START; use a short transaction-scoped PostgreSQL advisory lock only to serialize reconcilers; bind-probe the exact descriptor while the transaction is open; close rows only after successful OS-port acquisition; pin pg_catalog plus the resolved authority schema and skip malformed/conflicting metadata with diagnostics.
risks_and_mitigations: PostgreSQL session/server loss while model stays live: OS lease remains held, so reclaimer bind fails and no false STOP is written.
Two reconcilers race: deterministic transaction advisory lock plus holding the claimed OS socket through commit permits at most one closer.
Port reused by an unrelated process: bind fails and cleanup is delayed rather than falsely closing a live row.
Host permits two ordinary binds: acquisition self-test fails before artifact access.
Search-path or temporary-table shadowing: resolve one authority schema and transaction-locally pin pg_catalog, authority schema, then pg_temp.
research_basis_v2.validation_plan: Use real PostgreSQL plus real OS sockets to prove two live instances remain open, one released instance closes exactly once, loss of a PostgreSQL session while the OS holder remains alive closes zero rows, corrupt/conflicting metadata remains open while valid stale rows still reconcile, competing reconcilers serialize, and shadow schemas/temp tables receive no mutation.

validation_v2.fail_report: The session reclaimer calls append_reclaim_stop after a successful kill and reports stop_event_kind=STOP, but the ProcessLedgerWriter implementation delegates to ordinary append_stop. On a Full or Closed writer queue, enqueue records overflow telemetry and returns Ok without durably enqueuing STOP, so a killed process can be reported terminal while its row remains open. Separately, reclaim ownership contains only a 30-second timestamp; a slow kill permits a second claimant, and the first claimant can release the second claim by process UUID (ABA/double-action). The UserManual also says the boot reclaimer examines 32 groups while runtime caps it at 16.
remediation_plan: Reserve durable STOP authority before kill or persist a kill_succeeded_pending_stop state; do not report STOP until durable acknowledgement, and retry STOP persistence without re-killing.
Add a claimant UUID/fencing generation to claim, renewal/ownership checks, release WHERE claimant token, and STOP transition; test a kill blocked beyond claim TTL with two reclaimers.
Inject writer Full, writer Closed, and database-write failure after kill; assert no false STOP report and deterministic recovery.
Align the UserManual reclaim cap with runtime (16) or deliberately change the runtime constant, with a numeric parity assertion.

FAIL concurrency boundary: timestamp-only 30-second claim and UUID-only release permit ABA claim erasure/double action.

v5_proof_audit_2026_08_04.systemic_check: All 106 named-test proof references across all 23 MT contracts were scanned statically for this failure mode. Only these two are genuinely vacuous; the problem is confined to this restructured suite and is NOT packet-wide.

advisory_lock_database_scope_cascade_202.headline: DEFINITIVE EXPLANATION OF THE MIXED-SUITE CASCADE: PostgreSQL advisory locks are DATABASE-scoped, but this harness isolates tests by SCHEMA inside one shared database. Per-schema isolation therefore does NOT isolate the locks these code paths take, so parallel tests serialize and deadlock across schema boundaries.

the_two_facts_that_combine.1_locks_are_database_wide: pg_advisory_xact_lock keys live in a single per-DATABASE namespace. Two sessions in different schemas of the same database contend on the same key.
the_two_facts_that_combine.2_isolation_is_only_per_schema: Verified directly with psql: the managed cluster has ONE database (`handshake`) containing per-test schemas (mt013_<uuid>, and equivalents for other suites). Confirmed earlier when kernel_process_lifecycle was found once per test schema.

advisory_lock_database_scope_cascade_202.the_colliding_keyspace: swarm_orchestration/model_lane.rs::record_or_extend_run_tx takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended($1, 0)) keyed on run_id, AND swarm_orchestration/routing_execution.rs::lock_execution takes pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtextextended($1, 0)) keyed on execution_id. Same function, same salt (0), same database-wide namespace. record_or_extend_run_tx additionally takes a `SELECT ... FROM model_lane_runs WHERE run_id = $1 FOR UPDATE` row lock in the SAME caller-provided transaction.
why_this_produces_the_observed_symptoms: The failing/hanging SET changes between identical runs, because which test wins a lock depends on scheduling.

mt018_proposal_kind_crdt_message_with_approved_applied_proposal_is_admitted PASSED in one run and HUNG in the next with no change to it or to any CRDT code - it was queued behind another test's transaction, in a different schema.
Single-test runs (--exact) and single-threaded runs are reliable; that is exactly the configuration in which every fix this session was confirmed.

The observed blocking chain (holder idle-in-transaction after a scoped read -> a waiter on `transactionid` -> a waiter on `advisory`) is the model_lane run lock and the routing execution lock interacting.
advisory_lock_database_scope_cascade_202.relationship_to_the_other_root_cause: This is SEPARATE from, and compounded by, the transaction-across-generation defect recorded in transaction_across_generation_root_cause_2026_08_05. A transaction held open across inference makes the window enormous; database-wide advisory locks make that window affect UNRELATED tests in other schemas. Either alone is survivable; together they make the suite non-deterministic.

actionable_consequences.for_validation_now: Run mixed_model_lane_integration_pg_tests with `-- --test-threads=1` (or per-test --exact). A default-parallelism run is not reproducible and will accuse innocent tests. This is already recorded on MT-017, whose capstone declares this binary.
actionable_consequences.for_the_harness: True isolation requires a DATABASE per test (the task_owned_managed_postgres template mode already creates per-test databases) rather than a schema per test, OR the advisory keys must be namespaced per test schema so they cannot collide across concurrent tests.
actionable_consequences.for_the_product: Split the transaction at the generation await so no lane row and no advisory key is held across inference. Anchor identified: model_lane.rs::record_or_extend_run_tx is called from record_prepared_launch (line 245) inside a caller-controlled transaction.

advisory_lock_database_scope_cascade_202.verification_method: Two live pg_stat_activity/pg_blocking_pids samples taken DURING the hang windows, plus direct psql inspection of the cluster's database/schema layout. Not inferred from code reading alone.

twenty_seven_failures_narrowed_2026_08_0.headline: The 27 embedded_model_ledger_tests failures are NOT a malformed table, a missing migration, or a missing trigger. The authority relation is WELL-FORMED and satisfies every condition the guard checks. The failure is SEARCH-PATH VISIBILITY: the connection running the guard does not have the schema containing that relation on its search_path.
twenty_seven_failures_narrowed_2026_08_0.the_error: PROCESS_LEDGER_STORE: no migration-0021/0359-shaped, permanent, non-inherited, exact-runtime-owner-guard/RLS/rule-free kernel_process_lifecycle authority relation exists in the explicit PostgreSQL search path (process_ledger/reclaim.rs:808). This is the EMPTY-match branch, not the multiple-match branch.

what_was_verified_directly_with_psql.method: Ran the guard's OWN conditions as SQL against a real persisted kernel_process_lifecycle relation on the live managed cluster (oid 7338173).
what_was_verified_directly_with_psql.generated_expressions: PASSES - count = 4, and the four are exactly process_id -> process_uuid, adapter_id -> sandbox_adapter_id, spawned_at_utc -> started_at, stopped_at_utc -> stopped_at, as migration 0021/0359 requires.
what_was_verified_directly_with_psql.runtime_owner_guard: PASSES - trigger trg_kernel_process_runtime_owner_descriptor_guard is present and not internal.
what_was_verified_directly_with_psql.shape_flags: PASSES - relpersistence = p (permanent), relrowsecurity = f, relhassubclass = f (not inherited), relhasrules = f.

what_this_eliminates: ELIMINATED: 'the migration chain did not run in the isolated schema' - the relation exists with the full 0021/0359 shape.
ELIMINATED: 'the table shape drifted' - all four generated expressions and the exact single-column primary key are present.
ELIMINATED: 'the owner-guard trigger is missing' - it is there.

ELIMINATED: 'my migrations 0363/0364 broke it' - already separately proven; 0363 targets only model_lane_*, model_runtime_*, palmistry_durable_verifier and swarm_* tables and contains ZERO references to kernel_process_lifecycle.
twenty_seven_failures_narrowed_2026_08_0.what_remains: The store's connection search_path does not include the schema holding the relation when these tests run. Note this suite uses task_owned_managed_postgres (template mode: a DATABASE per test) while other suites use knowledge_pg (a SCHEMA per test) - the two modes place the relation differently, and the guard resolves candidates from the EXPLICIT search path only. That mode split is already recorded on this MT as an undocumented harness requirement.
twenty_seven_failures_narrowed_2026_08_0.concrete_next_step: Print the connection's actual `SHOW search_path` at the point the guard runs, and compare it to the schema the relation was created in. That single observation distinguishes 'search_path never set for this pool' from 'set to the wrong schema' from 'relation created in public while search_path excludes public'.
twenty_seven_failures_narrowed_2026_08_0.not_fixed_here: The fix belongs in the harness's pool/search_path wiring for this suite, not in product code. Changing it blind risks breaking the OTHER suites that depend on the schema-per-test mode, which are currently green.

twenty_seven_failures_ROOT_CAUSE_2026_08.headline: ROOT CAUSE FOUND: migration 0359's runtime-owner-guard TRIGGER is not created inside the isolated template-mode schema. The relation is otherwise perfect, so the authority guard's third condition fails and it reports zero matches.

evidence.enriched_error: search_path in force: [mt013_019fd05ffa0d7c30a7cda2cab2b2e08c]; kernel_process_lifecycle relations actually present in schemas: [mt013_019fd05ffa0d7c30a7cda2cab2b2e08c]. The relation IS in the search path and IS visible - so this is NOT the pool/search_path wiring fault previously suspected.
evidence.direct_psql_of_that_schema: relpersistence=p, relrowsecurity=f, relhassubclass=f, relhasrules=f (all correct). All FOUR generated expressions present (process_id->process_uuid, adapter_id->sandbox_adapter_id, spawned_at_utc->started_at, stopped_at_utc->stopped_at). TRIGGERS: NONE.
evidence.contrast: A storage_test_<uuid> schema on the external cluster HAS trg_kernel_process_runtime_owner_descriptor_guard and passes all three conditions. The template-mode schema does not. Same table, different creation path.

twenty_seven_failures_ROOT_CAUSE_2026_08.why_the_guard_fails: process_ledger/reclaim.rs requires primary_key_matches AND generated_expressions_match AND runtime_owner_guard_matches, then exactly one candidate. The first two pass; runtime_owner_guard_matches fails because the trigger is absent, leaving zero candidates and the '...exists in the explicit PostgreSQL search path' error.
twenty_seven_failures_ROOT_CAUSE_2026_08.correction_of_my_earlier_records: Two earlier entries in this MT are superseded. twenty_seven_failures_narrowed_2026_08_05 concluded the relation was well-formed and the fault was search-path visibility - that verification was performed against a storage_test_* schema from a DIFFERENT suite and mode, not against an mt013_* schema, and generalising from it was wrong. The enriched error then disproved the visibility theory outright.
twenty_seven_failures_ROOT_CAUSE_2026_08.known_fix_pattern_in_this_repo: This is the SAME defect class as migration 0363: a statement that resolves against `public` (or otherwise depends on search_path) silently does nothing when the harness runs each test in an isolated schema, while still recording the migration as applied. Migration 0364 fixed 0363 by resolving with quote_ident against the scoped table instead of a public-qualified name. Apply the same treatment to 0359's trigger creation.
twenty_seven_failures_ROOT_CAUSE_2026_08.verification_step_for_the_fix: After changing 0359, re-run any embedded_model_ledger_tests case in TEMPLATE mode and confirm the schema's kernel_process_lifecycle has trg_kernel_process_runtime_owner_descriptor_guard: SELECT tgname FROM pg_trigger t JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid=t.tgrelid JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid=c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname='<test schema>' AND c.relname='kernel_process_lifecycle' AND NOT t.tgisinternal;
twenty_seven_failures_ROOT_CAUSE_2026_08.diagnostic_left_in_product: The guard's empty-match error now prints the search_path in force and the schemas actually holding the relation, so this class of failure self-explains on any host instead of requiring a database inspector.

twenty_seven_failures_FINAL_ROOT_CAUSE_2.headline: FINAL. The template-mode test schema is NEVER MIGRATED. Migration 0359 did not partially apply - the migration machinery does not run in this mode at all. The schema is built by some other mechanism that creates TABLES but not functions, triggers, or 0359's columns.

evidence_live_psql_on_the_failing_schema.schema: mt013_019fd08ecba17bc287bd3b2468398777 (port 5563, created by the failing run itself)
evidence_live_psql_on_the_failing_schema.guard_function_kernel_process_runtime_ow: DOES NOT EXIST ANYWHERE IN THE DATABASE - not in the test schema, not in public.
evidence_live_psql_on_the_failing_schema._sqlx_migrations: DOES NOT EXIST IN ANY SCHEMA of this database.

twenty_seven_failures_FINAL_ROOT_CAUSE_2.why_this_settles_it: If the migration chain had run and only the trigger statement mis-resolved, _sqlx_migrations would exist and 0359's owner_runtime_instance_id column would be present. Neither is true. The absence of _sqlx_migrations anywhere proves sqlx migrations were never applied to this database.
supersedes_my_two_earlier_records: twenty_seven_failures_narrowed_2026_08_05 concluded 'relation is well-formed, fault is search-path visibility'. WRONG - that verification was run against a storage_test_* schema from a DIFFERENT suite and mode.

twenty_seven_failures_ROOT_CAUSE_2026_08_05 concluded 'migration 0359's trigger is not created in the template-mode schema, fix it like 0364 fixed 0363'. ALSO WRONG in its remedy: a new migration would accomplish NOTHING because nothing runs migrations in this mode. The observation that the trigger was missing was correct; the inference that 0359 had otherwise applied was not.
twenty_seven_failures_FINAL_ROOT_CAUSE_2.correct_fix_direction: Harness, not product, and not a migration. The template-mode path (tests/knowledge_pg_support.rs - task_owned_managed_postgres / create_migrated_template_database) must actually apply the migration chain to the template database before per-test schemas/databases are derived from it. Note create_migrated_template_database EXISTS in that file and is referenced at lines ~600-601; whether it is reached on this path is the thing to verify first.
twenty_seven_failures_FINAL_ROOT_CAUSE_2.do_NOT_do: Do not author a migration 0365 to re-create the trigger, and do not edit 0359. sqlx checksum-validates applied migrations, and in this mode there is no migration state to append to.
twenty_seven_failures_FINAL_ROOT_CAUSE_2.diagnostic_left_in_product: process_ledger/reclaim.rs's empty-match error now prints the search_path in force and the schemas holding the relation. That is what disproved the visibility theory and is worth keeping.
twenty_seven_failures_FINAL_ROOT_CAUSE_2.process_note: Three successive conclusions on this one defect were wrong before this one, each corrected by going back to live database evidence rather than reasoning from code. Anyone continuing should verify against a live failing schema before acting.
